item.description: The fans have yet to arrive at Levi’s Stadium. Game-day footballs are still pristine and no one knows what Bad Bunny has up his sleeve for the halftime show. But Emeryville resident Erin Fong has already won big: She designed the official theme art for Super Bowl LX. item.title: 30 Fun Things to Do This Week (2.09.26)
item.description: Be your own Valentine.This week, gift yourself Thai-Burmese food in Santa Rosa, music at SFJAZZ, and, of course, flowers. If love is in the air, so is artistic passion, with performances from the SF Grand Feature Film Orchestra, an immersive exhibit with Trina Michelle Robinson, and a love letter workshop. We’ve got ideas for the big V-day too, whether you want to strip down or light up.Jump ahead to this week's top events:See Little Shop of Horrors come to life with a live score in Napa Valley.

item.title: Modern Guide to Larkspur: Historic Marin Charm, Boutique Shops + Redwood Hiking
item.description: Though serene Larkspur is nestled against the Marin Hills just 20 minutes north of the city (adjust for rush hour traffic), it feels much farther away. Magnolia Avenue, in the heart of downtown, exudes a small-time appeal reminiscent of an early 1900s mill town, which, indeed, it was, with two sawmills that supplied lumber to the Presidio.Today, Larkspur is better known for its cute and quirky shops, historic landmarks, classy restaurants, and abundance of hiking trails. item.title: It’s show time at the Castro! Where to go before and after the curtain drops.
item.description: The work has been done and she’s ready for her reveal. This Tuesday, February 10th, marks the grand reopening of The Castro (formerly the Castro Theater) after two years of thoughtful renovations to preserve the character and add much-needed improvements. To celebrate this milestone, the legendary Sam Smith will host a twenty-day residency, To Be Free—which sold out minutes after it was announced. item.title: Modern Guide to Mission Bay: San Francisco’s Bright New Waterfront Neighborhood
item.description: Mission Bay wasn’t always one of the city’s most sought-after neighborhoods. Previously more regaled for its industrial monuments than its potential for living and playing, recent years have transformed the biotech hub into a dense, walkable, sunny neighborhood full of parks, restaurants, and more. item.description: Wine sales have been dipping as Gen Z and millennials either quit drinking, cut back on alcohol, or choose options a little less wine-y. item.title: First Taste: Rich Table's laidback spinoff RT Bistro is SF's first best new restaurant of 2026.
item.description: It takes awhile for a brand new restaurant to work out the kinks.
